items.title: 'If you buy Kyle, you get Kyle': Sandilands dispute returns to court
items.description: Kyle Sandilands and Jackie 'O' Henderson have separately launched legal proceedings following the termination of their $100 million contracts.

items.title: Baby boomers beware: Labor is reading the room on generational inequity
items.description: The Albanese government is reading the room when it comes to intergenerational equity ahead of the May 12 budget.

items.title: What happened when I messaged the number threatening slain reporter
items.description: Talks in Washington are set against a backdrop of decades-long disputes and deep mistrust, but at least they're happening.

items.title: Live: Australia secures 100 million litres more diesel as Trump extends Israel-Lebanon ceasefire
items.description: Fuel giants Ampol and BP will deliver the extra shipments, with about half of it being directed to regional Queensland. Follow live.

items.title: Ben Roberts-Smith confirms Anzac Day plans
items.description: Ben Roberts-Smith confirms he will be attending Anzac Day services tomorrow, saying he intends to pay his respects, one week on from his release on bail.

items.title: Gag order lifted on identity of ex-soldier who murdered Nick Martin
items.description: The former soldier who publicly assassinated ex-Rebels bikie boss Nick Martin at Perth Motorplex in 2020 can be publicly identified for the first time, after he successfully overturned a court order suppressing his identity.

items.title: End to 'let it rip' NDIS provider spending and claims submitted 'on serviettes'
items.description: NDIS Minister Mark Butler will end the practice of handwritten invoices, providers without qualifications and a "let it rip" market of profiteering operators. But the sector warns changes must be navigated carefully.

items.title: 'Genuinely speechless': Appeal board's stunning claim in homophobia case
items.description: The appeal board in the Lance Collard homophobia case says homophobic and racist language is commonplace in the AFL due to the "highly competitive" nature of the game.

items.title: 'They deserve death': Officer used dispatch system to monitor police wife
items.description: Text messages read in court set out how a Tasmania Police officer monitored his wife's movements, including via an internal dispatching system, as part of a 15-month family violence matter.

items.title: Centenarian bugler prepares to play Last Post for 92nd time
items.description: A Boort centenarian is preparing to blow his bugle this Anzac Day at local schools and the RSL.

items.title: Mapping the most critical shipping lanes in the world
items.description: Oil prices have spiked since the Strait of Hormuz was closed. With about 90 per cent of all traded goods shipped by sea, what are the other key shipping lanes in the world?

items.title: Failing on social mobility 'is inefficiency with a human face'
items.description: Is reducing inequality and increasing social mobility one of Australia's best paths to improving our lacklustre economic productivity performance?

items.title: Live: ASX 200 down after Wall Street losses, oil prices spike again
items.description: Oil prices are spiking again on global markets, and the ASX is trading in negative territory on the final day of the week. It comes after the Nasdaq shed almost 1 per cent. Follow the day's events and insights as they happen with our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Pentagon awards $276m AUKUS contract funded by Australia
items.description: The US Department of Defense announces the first major submarine contract to deliver on the AUKUS security deal.

items.title: Tradwives, gangsters and one very special dog: April's 10 best books
items.description: This month's top picks include new works from Steve Toltz and Colm Tóibín, a satire inspired by Yellowface and an investigation into the death of a London teen who masqueraded as the son of a Russian oligarch.

items.title: Jane Fonda was in her 40s when she changed the way we exercise
items.description: In the 1980s, the fitness industry as we know it was just getting started. One of the most important people in developing the way we exercise today was Jane Fonda, who released a best-selling aerobics video in 1982.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: Trump's eleventh-hour announcement, a disabled bird and a speedy humanoid robot
items.description: It's Friday, and that means it's time to test your news knowledge from the past seven days. Were you paying attention this week?

items.title: Michael Tilson Thomas, 12-time Grammy-winning conductor, dies aged 81
items.description: The celebrated conductor led the San Francisco Symphony for 25 years, and co-founded the New World Symphony.

items.title: Police dismiss claims organised crime linked to farmer's murder
items.description: Fake images and false claims about Richard Wills's death are circulating on social media, prompting police to speak out about the investigation into the 65-year-old farmer's murder.

items.title: Teen killer of Qld grandmother loses sentence appeal
items.description: The 16-year sentence handed to the teenager who murdered south east Queensland woman Vyleen White has been upheld by the state's Court of Appeal.

items.title: Dozen more possible human burial sites found at Rottnest Island church
items.description: Authorities believe there may be a dozen more unmarked Aboriginal burial sites near where human remains were found on Western Australia's tourist haven Rottnest Island earlier this month.

items.title: Perth woman warns about pedicure safety after severe infection
items.description: Kyla Willcox says she almost lost her toe from a potentially fatal infection after having a pedicure at a Perth nail salon.

items.title: Hundreds of fishing boats sit idle off southern China — but they're not there to fish
items.description: Off China's southern coast, hundreds of fishing boats sit idle. The crews aren't there to fish, but rather to "maintain presence" as part of a shadowy, state-funded fleet.

items.title: 'This is now terminal': UK braces for prospect of sixth PM in seven years
items.description: Sir Keir Starmer, who led Labour to a landslide general election victory in July 2024, has become so unpopular that even some colleagues are framing his demise as a case of not if, but when.

items.title: Prince Harry urges Putin to 'stop this war' on visit to Ukraine
items.description: Prince Harry makes a surprise visit to Kyiv, urging Russia's President Vladimir Putin to end the war and calling on US President Donald Trump to show leadership to help resolve the conflict in Ukraine.
